summary: Morgana (Earth Trends Lab) is a bilingual web tool that turns NASA climate records into clear answers about how local climate is changing. We used daily 2-meter air temperature (maximum, mean and minimum) from NASA's MERRA-2 reanalysis, obtained through Giovanni, for the Piura region of Peru from 1980 to 2026. Morgana cleans the data, builds annual series and estimates the trend with the Theil–Sen slope and a 95% confidence interval, testing significance with Mann–Kendall corrected for autocorrelation. For Piura, mean temperature rises about +0.163 °C per decade (95% CI +0.029 to +0.286; p = 0.0184). It also offers anomalies against a 1991–2020 baseline, a variable scanner, maps, short-term forecasts and an AI assistant that explains results in plain language. It answers the Earth System Trend Detective challenge by making evidence of change accessible to farmers and to anyone without statistics training, and it lays groundwork for future El Niño analysis.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Morgana (Earth Trends Lab) lets a user pick a date range and a variable (today: temperature) and then investigates the record. It answers four questions: What changes? Where? How much? Is it significant? Results appear in tabs: Results, Map, Scanner, Anomalies and Forecast. A built-in assistant named Morgana explains the numbers in plain language, in Spanish or English.

HOW IT WORKS

1. We downloaded three daily time series from NASA Giovanni (MERRA-2, product M2SDNXSLV v5.12.4): 2-meter air temperature maximum, mean and minimum, area-averaged over Piura, from 1980-01-01 to 2026-10-01.

2. Temperatures are converted from Kelvin to °C and the three series are aligned on common dates.

3. Annual means are computed only for years with at least 80% daily coverage (1980-2025; the partial year 2026 is excluded).

4. The trend is estimated with the Theil-Sen slope and a 95% confidence interval. Significance uses the Mann-Kendall test with an AR(1) autocorrelation correction. Comparisons across variables or pixels use Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate control.

5. Anomalies are computed against a fixed 1991-2020 monthly reference. If the reference period is incomplete, no other period is substituted.

6. Complementary tools: K-means and DBSCAN clustering, Isolation Forest for atypical patterns, Pettitt and ΔBIC for level shifts, and short-term forecasting with forward validation.

RESULT FOR PIURA

Mean temperature rises +0.163 °C per decade (95% CI +0.029 to +0.286; Mann-Kendall p = 0.0184). Daily maximum and minimum temperatures also trend upward.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

Morgana brings NASA data closer to everyone who needs it, in an accessible form. Our primary audience is farmers in Piura. The same approach can be extended to other regions, other variables (pressure is marked as coming soon) and, in the future, to analysis that supports the prevention of natural disasters such as El Niño.

TOOLS

Python, Streamlit, pandas, NumPy, SciPy, scikit-learn, Matplotlib, xarray, netCDF4, h5netcdf, Dask, earthaccess, pytest. The in-app assistant uses the Anthropic Claude API.

WHAT MAKES IT CREATIVE

It frames raw climate statistics as a "trend detective" investigation, explains results in plain language, and is bilingual. The statistics code was written by our team, and the app states its own limits openly: short series, autocorrelation, reanalysis is not field observation, and a trend is not a cause.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

Data coverage thresholds, autocorrelation, multiple comparisons, a fixed climatological baseline, spatial dependence between pixels, and the fact that results are exploratory and need sensitivity analysis before publication.

USE OF AI

The statistical analysis and application code were written by hand by our team. AI was used in two places only. (1) The visual design and the functionality of the user interface were built with AI assistance: ChatGPT for the aesthetics and Google Antigravity for the interface functionality. (2) The in-app assistant, Morgana, calls the Anthropic Claude API with tools to explain results; if the AI service is unavailable or its answer cannot be verified, the app shows a prepared offline response instead.
